solves: Lets the person choose one option in a small group of options that exclude each other, all visible at the same time; checking one unchecks the others.
use_when: When the options exclude each other: payment method, employment type, work shift.
When the group is small and fits the screen, with two to five options.
When every option must stay visible at the same time, so the person compares before choosing.
Always in a group of two or more, with one option checked when there is a reasonable default.
do_not_use_when: When the person can check more than one option: use nph-checkbox.
For a single option, alone: either options are missing, or the piece is nph-checkbox.
With more than five options: use nph-select.
When the person needs to uncheck by clicking again: offer a None option, or use nph-checkbox.
To mix radios and checkboxes in the same group.

checked.constraint: The current state, the Figma marcado. The checked attribute is the initial state and the one form.reset() returns to; a later change of the attribute moves the current state only while neither the person nor code changed checked. Setting it from code unchecks the other radios of the group and fires no event. There is no indeterminate.

name.constraint: The group and the key in the form. Radios with the same non-empty name, in the same root and with the same form owner, are one group. It reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host; an empty name writes no attribute. Without a name, the radio is a group of one and warns in development.

value.constraint: What the checked radio submits, under name. Only the checked radio of a group enters the form. The default, on, is also written as the attribute, and removing the attribute gives back on. A radio that is not drawn submits nothing.

text.constraint: The visible text, already localized; it is also the accessible name. Without it, the piece is only the 24 by 24 circle: the Figma property that shows the text, turned off.

label.constraint: The accessible name when there is no text, never visible. Without text, label, aria-label or aria-labelledby on the host (an empty or blank one counts as none), the radio draws nothing and emits console.error in development. With text, label is not used.

invalid.constraint: The error border, checked or not. Visual only: aria-invalid is not supported on the radio role, and the error sentence belongs to nph-field. disabled wins over it.

disabled.constraint: The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, text included, out of the Tab order and the arrow keys, and the click does not check it. A disabled fieldset around the radio does the same. It wins over invalid.

input.constraint: The native input event, fired on the host when the person checks the radio: it bubbles and crosses the shadow root. Read event.target.value. A change from code never fires it.

change.constraint: The native change event, fired on the host right after input, when the person checks the radio: it bubbles and does not cross the shadow root. A change from code never fires it.

checked.choose_when: checked for the option chosen, unchecked for the others. One option checked when there is a reasonable default.
do_not_combine_with: two checked radios in the same group: the last one wins.

text.choose_when: With text, always, except when the name is already in the context, such as a card in nph-rich-option, where the radio is the circle alone with label.

default.token: color/background fill and color/input border; checked, color/primary fill and color/primary-foreground dot
default.changes_for_user: Unchecked is an empty circle; checked is filled, with the dot. The border stays color/input in both.

hover.token: color/input-hover border; checked, state/hover-opacity on the circle
hover.changes_for_user: The border goes one step up, so the circle responds to the mouse; it has no size change.

focus.token: focus/border border and focus/halo halo, focus/ring-width, radius/full
focus.changes_for_user: Keyboard only: the border turns focus/border and the halo covers the 24 by 24 touch area.

error.token: status/error border; with focus, focus/halo-error halo
error.changes_for_user: The border turns status/error, checked or not; the checked fill stays color/primary. The sentence is in nph-field.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole piece, text included, loses opacity and stops responding. It does not combine with error: disabled wins.

business_rules: Radios with the same name, in the same root and with the same form owner, are one group: checking one unchecks the others.
The person never unchecks a radio by clicking it again: a click on the checked radio changes nothing and fires no event, and the click still bubbles.
Only the person checking a radio, by click, Space or an arrow key, fires input and change; setting checked from code never fires them.
One Tab stop per group, on the checked radio or, with none checked, on the first one that responds; the arrow keys move the focus and check, wrapping, skipping a disabled radio.
Only the checked radio enters the form, as name=value; form.reset() returns each radio to its checked attribute.
Without a name, or alone in its group, the radio still renders and warns in development: a radio never shows alone.
domain_errors: invalid: the group failed validation. Every radio shows the status/error border; the sentence that says what to fix is the error message of nph-field.

tokens.circle_border: color/input; hover color/input-hover; error status/error; focus focus/border
tokens.dot: color/primary-foreground; 8 by 8, the circle minus space/inline-tight on each side
tokens.touch_area: the circle plus space/inline-tight on each side: 24 by 24

ai_hints: Use nph-radio when the options exclude each other and there are two to five of them; if the person can check more than one, use nph-checkbox; with more than five, nph-select.
Give every radio of a group the same name and its own value; put the group inside an nph-field, which names it and carries the error message.
Read the chosen value from event.target.value on change; do not listen to click.
Put the checked attribute on the default option; it is also the state the form returns to on reset.
Set invalid on every radio of the group, together with the error message in nph-field; never leave a radio red without a sentence.
Use the circle alone, with label, only where the name is already in the context, such as a card of nph-rich-option.
Offer a None option when the person may want no choice: a radio cannot be unchecked by clicking again.

accessibility.semantics: The host is the control: role radio, with aria-checked and aria-disabled, through ElementInternals. There is no inner input. The group, role radiogroup with its name, comes from nph-field.
accessibility.accessible_name: The text is the name of the control. Without text, label is the name; aria-label or aria-labelledby on the host also count. The group gets the name of nph-field.
keyboard: Tab enters the group on the checked radio or, with none checked, on the first one that responds; the next Tab leaves the group.
Arrow down and arrow right move to the next radio and check it, wrapping; arrow up and arrow left, to the previous one.
A disabled radio is out of the Tab order and the arrow keys skip it; so is a radio hidden by display: none, on itself or on an ancestor.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only: the circle border turns focus/border and a focus/halo halo covers the 24 by 24 touch area, fully round. With error, the border stays status/error and the halo is focus/halo-error. A mouse click does not show it.
accessibility.contrast: The circle outline in color/input: 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark; the text, 21:1 and 14.73:1. The test measures the dot on the checked fill and the error border in every brand and scheme. Known limit: in light mode of the default brand, focus/border measures 2.92:1 against the halo, as design.md records.
accessibility.color_alternative: The border says the state and the fill and the dot say the choice; the error has the sentence in nph-field.

invalid_combinations: No text, no label, no aria-label and no aria-labelledby — the radio draws nothing.
invalid with disabled — disabled wins: no error border, and it is not a console error.
A radio without name, or alone in its group — it renders and warns in development.
Two checked radios in the same group — the last one wins.
anti_patterns: Using radios when the person can check more than one option.
More than five options in a radio group.
Expecting the person to uncheck by clicking again.
Mixing radios and checkboxes in the same group.
A red radio without a sentence that explains the error.
Painting the circle or the dot by hand.
